title: Keep a practice log

body.heading: Memory lies, logs do not
paragraphs: Ask a musician what they practised last Tuesday and you will get a shrug. Practice feels formless from the inside, which makes progress hard to see and easy to doubt.
A log fixes that. Two or three honest lines per session create a record you can trust: the piece that finally clicked, the drill that is not working, the pattern in your best days.

body.heading: Three lines are enough
paragraphs: After each session, write: what I did, what got easier or clearer, and what I will start with next time. That last line is the treasure: it removes the cold start from your next session entirely.
Review the log every few weeks. You will spot plateaus earlier, notice which practice actually pays off, and have solid evidence, on doubtful days, that the work is adding up.

takeaway: Three lines after each session: what you did, what improved, what comes next.
